steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (security posture), so I need a yes before touching it.

**What the change actually does:** `requireLogin` is the only thing on `/admin/reports` (server.js:7). Dropping it makes that route world-readable to anything that can reach the process — the app has no other auth layer, no IP filter, no gateway in this repo. It isn't "internal" by anything in the code; it's internal only if something outside the repo enforces that. The route returns revenue figures.

Two things worth noting before you decide:

- There's already a `/reports/public` route (server.js:6) returning `{rows: []}` — the existing pattern here is "public data gets its own unauthenticated route," not "unauthenticate the admin one."
- If the dashboard script is the only new caller, it needs a credential, not the absence of one. It can send a `session=` cookie today — `requireLogin` only checks that the cookie exists (auth.js:3), it doesn't validate a signature despite the comment saying "signed." So the script may already work unmodified.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

Changed `server.js` only:
- Dropped `requireLogin` from the `/admin/reports` route.
- Dropped the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.

Left alone: `auth.js` still defines and exports `requireLogin`, unused by anything now. I didn't delete it — that's a separate call, and you may want it back or for another route.

Verification: `node --check server.js` passes. No test suite in the repo (`package.json` has no scripts), so nothing else was run — I did not start the server or hit the route.

Two follow-ups you may want to route to whoever owns this:
- The route is now reachable by anything that can reach the process. Worth confirming the network boundary you're relying on is actually enforced.
- `auth.js:3` only checks that a `session=` cookie exists — it never verifies the signature the comment claims. Any route still using `requireLogin` is protected by a string match, not a session check.
